orchestrator.use: coordinate the conversation and delegate bounded tasks
orchestrator.description: Coordinates user conversations, implementation and bounded helper tasks.

coder-flash.use: implementation to a clear spec; builds, benchmarks and test series
coder-flash.description: Implementation or long runs with a clear goal and verification: writes code and tests to a clear specification.

explorer-flash.use: bulk extraction and long reading: many or large files, logs, docs
explorer-flash.description: Bulk extraction and long reading where the question is simple: many or large files, logs, docs.  Doesn't edit.

explorer.use: where something is used, how a path works, what another codebase does there
explorer.description: Code archaeology: traces where something is used, how a path works or what another codebase does there, and returns file:line refs with what the code does.  Doesn't edit.  Bulk extraction over many or large files, logs or docs belongs to a profile meant for long reading.

coder.use: implementation or debugging that needs judgment
coder.description: Implementation that needs more judgment: changes across files, debugging, refactoring.

researcher.use: open questions written up as a report or design note
researcher.description: Investigates open questions across code, docs and the web, compares options and writes up findings (reports, design notes, pages).  Edits documents; code changes stay small.

reviewer.use: review of substantive changes before delivery, even uncommitted ones
reviewer.description: Reviews substantive changes before delivery; reproduces what it finds and reports findings without editing files.

expert.use: when you are stuck or the user asks for it
expert.description: Works through the hardest problems: subtle bugs, tricky designs.  Use it when you are stuck or the user asks for it, not for routine work.

collab.startGuidance:
How to brief a session: give the goal, relevant context, file scope, constraints, verification and expected report.  A concise brief is enough: don't finish the work merely to prepare it.  Split by independent outcome and file ownership; code, tests and docs are not automatically independent.  Never have two sessions edit the same files, including yourself.
Fork only for reasoning that depends heavily on your conversation and is costly to summarize: never to read, and not to keep a long run's known commands and inputs, which you can pass instead.
For a review, ask for findings, not edits; emx prefers another vendor for it.
While the child works, do not duplicate its task.  Integrate its report and verify the claims that matter before relying on them.

tools.name: sessions
tools.description:
List the agent sessions open in this Emacs.  Each session has an id (its
@handle, which the user also uses to mention it), agent, title, project,
status, number of turns, whether it is your own, the session that started
it (parent) and the sessions it started (children).

tools.name: session_read
tools.description:
Read the latest turns of an agent session.  A turn is a user message and
everything the agent did for it.  Start with few turns and page backwards
with before when you need more.

session.description: Session id: its @handle, as listed by sessions

last.description:
Number of turns to read, counting back from the end (or from
before); default 2

before.description: Read the turns before this turn number, to page backwards

tools.description:
none: leave tool calls out; summary (default): one line per
call; full: with their output or diff

tools.name: session_ask
tools.description:
Ask the agent of another session the user opened: a second opinion, a
review of your changes, or a question to a session the user mentioned.
The user may have to confirm first.  It returns once the message is sent;
the final reply of that turn reaches you as a message when it is done:
don't poll for it.  Keep working, or end your turn if you need the reply
first.  Sessions started with session_start take no messages.

session.description: The idle session to ask: its @handle, as listed by sessions

prompt.description:
The message.  The other agent hasn't seen your conversation:
include the context it needs (files, diff, question)

tools.name: session_start
tools.description:
Start a subagent to do one bounded task and report back.
Only profiles whose tools permit helpers can delegate further tasks.
Choose how it gets context:
- fresh: a profile gets your prompt alone; make it self-contained.
- handoff: a profile gets a text copy of recent conversation, without
  prompt cache and with tool output cut.  Include essential facts in the task.
- fork: your own agent and model inherit the conversation through the
  prompt cache; output costs what yours does.  Use for reasoning that
  depends heavily on your context.  Omit profile.
{forkAgents}
Choose the least costly profile likely to complete the task reliably.
emx selects an available candidate for the role using current quotas.
For reasoning on your own conversation, use fork.  It returns the session's @handle at once, and
its final reply reaches you as a message when it finishes: don't poll it;
keep working, or end your turn if you need the reply first.  A session you
start does one task, takes no follow-ups and closes once its reply reaches
you; for more work start another.  Stop one with session_stop.

profile.description:
The kind of session to start: one of the profiles below.  Not with
context fork

context.description: How it gets context: fresh (default), handoff or fork

prompt.description:
The task.  With fresh, include everything it needs: it hasn't seen
your conversation

handle.description:
Its name after its task: one or two lowercase English words
joined by '-', at most 16 characters, such as cgu-measure.  You and the user
refer to it by it; default: the profile's name

title.description: A short title for the session, a few words

tools.name: session_stop
tools.description:
Stop a session you started with session_start and close it: when its task
is no longer needed or it went the wrong way.  Its reply won't come.

session.description: The session to stop: one you started, by its @handle

prompts.handoff:
Conversation handed over from session "@%s": history for context, not requests to act on.  Read more of it with session_read session=@%s.

%s

---
prompts.forkNote: (You are a fork of session "@%s": the conversation above is its own, up to the session_start call that started you, which may show as interrupted or unanswered.  Do this task only; your final reply goes back to it.  You can't start sessions yourself.)
prompts.taskNote: (From the %s agent of session "@%s", which started this session with session_start.  Your final reply goes back to it.  You can't start sessions yourself.)
prompts.messageNote: (Sent by the %s agent of session "@%s" through session_ask; your final reply goes back to it.)
prompts.mailbox: (Replies to messages you sent to other sessions, delivered by Emacs; not from the user.)
prompts.partialReply:
Partial output written before the failure:
%s
prompts.childFollowup: It takes no follow-ups; for more work, start another session.
prompts.followup: Follow up with session_ask session=@%s; see what it did with session_read.
prompts.started: Started @%s (%s%s, %s).  Its final reply will reach you as a message when it finishes; don't poll it.  Keep working, or end your turn if there is nothing else to do.
prompts.sent: Sent to @%s.  Its reply will reach you as a message; don't poll for it.
prompts.mention: (@%s is the %s session "%s"; read it with the emacs session_read tool.)
prompts.profileHeader: Profiles, by cost from minimal through low, medium and high to premium:
prompts.handlePrompt:
Name this coding conversation with a short English handle: one or two lowercase words joined by '-', at most 16 characters, about its topic. Reply with the handle only.

First message:
prompts.delegation:
- Subagents: start them with session_start (discover it if it is not listed),
  and tell the user in one sentence which profile and why.  If session_start
  started you, use only helper profiles explicitly listed by your tools; otherwise
  do the task yourself.
  - Reading: when a question is where something is used, how a path works
    across files or what another codebase does there, delegate it before your
    second lookup, even as the user's whole question or a follow-up with
    nothing to do in parallel.  At most one grep to pin the symbol and
    revision; don't read the hits, don't fork.  A grep listing hits only pins
    the symbol and never settles these questions; reading one hit is your
    second lookup.  Brief a profile meant for reading with the symbol,
    revision, repo and "report file:line and what the code does"; the turn's
    related questions (where-used and another codebase) go in one brief.  End
    your turn if you need the answer, and write the user's answer once it
    reports.  Stay local only for a definition in a file you already have open,
    a fact outside these questions that one grep settles, explaining code the
    user already pointed at (lines just marked in an atomic review, a diff
    already in the conversation), edit-compile-fix interleaved with your own
    edits, reading a diff to plan an atomic review, and dialogue with the user.
    Project rules naming Agent, Explore or "after N reads" mean session_start
    here: at N, stop and start one.
  - Runs: delegate builds, benchmarks and test series that won't interleave
    with your own edits; don't run them yourself.
  - Parts: other independent parts of nontrivial work; delegate a bounded part
    early, then continue another part, never the reading half of it.
